ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, D, C are on the same straight line, D is located between A and C; B is above the straight line, AB, BD, BC are connected; at point C, ∠BCD = 70° is marked. Reasoning: In triangle BCD, the problem gives BD = DC, so triangle BCD is an isosceles triangle, with base BC, therefore the base angles ∠DBC and ∠BCD are equal. Given ∠BCD = 70°, so ∠DBC = 70°. By the sum of the interior angles of a triangle, ∠BDC = 180° - 70° - 70° = 40°. Since A, D, C are collinear, rays DA and DC are opposite rays, therefore ∠ADB and ∠BDC form a pair of linear angles, and their sum is 180°. So ∠ADB = 180° - 40° = 140°.

By the triangle angle sum, ∠BDC=180°−70°−70°=40°. From the image/text, A, D, C are collinear with D on AC, so ∠ADB and ∠BDC form a linear pair. Thus ∠ADB=180°−40°=140°.

method.method_draft: View ∠ADB directly as an exterior angle of triangle BCD at D, because A, D, C are collinear and ray DA is the extension of ray DC. Since BD=DC, triangle BCD is isosceles, so the base angles opposite equal sides are equal: ∠DBC=∠BCD=70°. By the exterior angle theorem, exterior angle ∠ADB equals the sum of the two remote interior angles of triangle BCD: ∠ADB=∠DBC+∠BCD=70°+70°=140°.
